appearance_facts.fact: Title reads 'Increasing Clean Grid Output from 2018 to 2023' in large bold black text.
Vertical axis label 'Grid Output (GWh)' is printed vertically.
Horizontal axis label 'Year' is centered below the year ticks.
A single solid blue line connects six data points, one per year from 2018 to 2023.
The line starts high in 2018, drops to its lowest point in 2019, rises to a peak in 2020, falls in 2021, and remains nearly flat and slightly decreasing through 2023.
The 2018 point is the second-highest on the line, positioned just above the 2,800 gridline level.
The 2019 point is the minimum of the series, located at the 2,400 gridline level.
The 2020 point is the maximum of the series, located slightly above the 2,800 gridline level.

printed_facts.fact: The printed title states 'Increasing Clean Grid Output from 2018 to 2023'.

uncertain: The printed title claims 'Increasing' output, but the plotted line shows a drop from 2018 to 2019, a peak in 2020, and a subsequent decline/plateau through 2023, so the title's direction conflicts with the visible line trend.
Exact GWh values for 2021, 2022, and 2023 are not numerically labeled; they must be read visually from the line's position relative to the 2,400 and 2,800 gridlines.
It is not specified whether 'overall dashboard trend' should be judged by the title text, the net change from 2018 to 2023, or the recent multi-year direction of the line.
